title: Sable Logistics POC — latency & throughput sweep notes
summary: Notes and raw results from the 2026-04 latency/throughput sweep run with Sable Logistics during onsite workshop. Goal: characterize tail latency and token throughput for driver-assistance NLP flows, evaluate cost trade-offs across model variants and quantization, and produce deployment recommendation for a mixed-latency SLA (p95 < 300ms for short queries, p95 < 800ms for long queries during peak).
experiment_setup: Environment: Redwood Dedicated test pool (isolated), three GPU node types: A100-80GB (p4d-like), A10G (g5-like), and T4 (legacy). Runtime: inference engine v2.9.3 with continuous batching and KV prefix caching enabled. Model variants: rwin-1.3B (baseline distilled), rwin-7B, rwin-13B (float32), rwin-13B-8bit (Q8), rwin-13B-4bit (Q4), and rwin-13B-distilled-qa (smaller decoder tweaks). Sequence lengths: short (20–80 tokens), medium (80–250), long (250–700). Typical prompt: route+context + 1–2 messages, avg ~120 tokens input, avg output 60 tokens. Load generator: locust-based harness with realistic interarrival distributions (bursty daytime peaks), concurrency sweeps: 10, 50, 100, 200 req/s. Batching parameters swept: max_batch_size {1, 4, 8, 16}, batch_wait_ms {2, 10, 25}. Prefix caching toggled (on/off) for repeated route lookups. Cost calc: GPU-hour cost estimates from finance (A100 $3.20/hr equivalent for billing), tokenization + per-request overhead included in per-1M-token estimate.
workload_profile: Sable use-case: driver assistant used at route start and on-demand for instructions. Two main traffic patterns: (1) micro-interactions — short prompts requesting next-turn instructions (median response 40 tokens) with strict latency target, bursty at route start (30s windows); (2) contextual planning — medium/long prompts including route history and constraints (150-450 tokens) with relaxed latency. Peak target: sustain ~200 req/s for micro-interactions while keeping p95 under 300ms for short flows. Baseline failure mode: long planning requests blocking small ones if batching not tuned or if model too slow.
experiments:
Run 1: baseline (rwin-1.3B) on T4 nodes: concurrency up to 200 req/s. Observed p50/p95/p99 (short): 45ms / 180ms / 420ms. Throughput tokens/sec: ~220k (aggregate). Notes: low cost but poor quality on planning prompts; tail p99 hit 420ms due to occasional GC spikes in runtime.

Run 2: rwin-7B on A10G (mixed): batch_size 8, wait 10ms, prefix caching on. Short p50/p95/p99: 28ms / 120ms / 300ms. Medium p95: 560ms. Throughput tokens/sec: ~480k. Cost per 1M tokens: ~$85 (est). Quality: much better than 1.3B.

Run 3: rwin-13B float32 on A100: batch_size 8, wait 10ms, prefix caching on. Short p50/p95/p99: 24ms / 98ms / 210ms. Medium p95: 420ms. Long p95: 780ms. Throughput tokens/sec: ~1.1M. Cost per 1M tokens: ~$220.

Run 4: rwin-13B-8bit on A100: same batching. Short p50/p95/p99: 26ms / 105ms / 240ms. Medium p95: 450ms. Throughput tokens/sec: ~1.05M. Cost per 1M tokens: ~$95 (after quantization efficiency factor). Note: quality regression minor on some planning completions; flagged by Lina.

Run 5: rwin-13B-4bit on A100: lower mem, batch_size 16 possible. Short p50/p95/p99: 30ms / 135ms / 360ms. Medium p95: 620ms. Throughput tokens/sec: ~1.3M (higher tokens/sec but worse latency tail). Cost per 1M tokens: ~$60. Quality: more pronounced degradations on numeric/table outputs.

Run 6: adaptive routing simulation: short flows sent to rwin-7B on A10G, long flows to rwin-13B-8bit on A100; fallback policy to rwin-1.3B under overload. Observed end-to-end p95 (short): 110ms; p95 (long): 530ms. System sustained 200 req/s bursts with <1% error rate. Cost blended: ~$120 per 1M tokens.

Micro-observations: batching wait 10ms seems sweet-spot for this workload; 25ms introduces higher client latency for short flows. Prefix caching reduces medium/long cost by ~18% and p95 by ~12% for repeated route-context retrievals.
results_summary:
Key metrics (short flow target = p95 < 300ms): rwin-1.3B meets latency but fails planning quality; rwin-7B is a balanced cost/latency/quality option; rwin-13B float32 provides best quality and lowest p95 but at high cost; rwin-13B-8bit yields near-13B quality with ~55% cost reduction and acceptable latency; rwin-13B-4bit gives best tokens/sec but worsened tail latency and quality. Adaptive routing (small->7B, long->13B-8bit) achieves SLA and reduces cost vs full-13B deployment.

Tail risks: p99 spikes tied to node maintenance and occasional recompile/kernels in runtime; observed one ~3s outage when a node loader recompiled kernels during first warmup run — mitigated by warming and persistent compilation caches.

Reliability: KV/prefix cache hit rates directly correlated with medium-flow latency — cache eviction policies need tuning for per-driver context retention (suggest 10k entries per node).
cost_analysis:
Assumptions: A100 equivalent $3.20/hr, A10G equivalent $1.10/hr, T4 $0.45/hr; tokenization + infra overhead adds $0.12 per 1k requests. Costs reported are approximate and for decision-making only.

Per-1M-token estimates (approx):
- rwin-1.3B @ T4: $18
- rwin-7B @ A10G: $85
- rwin-13B float @ A100: $220
- rwin-13B Q8 @ A100: $95
- rwin-13B Q4 @ A100: $60

Notes: Q8 measured giving best cost-quality tradeoff. Q4 cheaper but observed quality degradations on numeric/structured outputs which are relevant for Sable (ETAs, cost tables). Adaptive routing reduces blended cost to ~$120/1M while meeting latency SLOs. Potential ops savings if we reserve capacity (Dedicated) for A100 pool — 15–25% depending on commit term.
recommendations:
Short term (next 1–4 weeks):
- Pilot deployment: adaptive-routing config (short->rwin-7B on A10G, long->rwin-13B-Q8 on A100) with prefix caching enabled and batch_size=8, batch_wait_ms=10.
- Warmup hooks: run periodic warmup compiled kernels during maintenance windows to avoid live first-request spikes.
- Cache tuning: increase per-node prefix cache retention to 10k entries, LRU with pinning for route-start contexts.

Medium term (1–3 months):
- Run a 2-week canary in customer's dedicated pool with traffic mirroring at 10% to validate quality regressions observed in Q8.
- Integrate eval suite (existing Redwood Optimize harness) with Sable prompt set for regression alerts.

Long term:
- Consider model distillation work to bring planning quality of rwin-7B closer to 13B for cost-sensitive customers.
- Contract discussion: propose A100 committed burst capacity (Dedicated) — will reduce per-token by 15% on top of quantization savings.
